title: Phase 3: Supported public import boundaries
status_detail: Inactive Phase 3; package-specific export and compatibility child Tasks remain deferred until the preceding policy and conformance results exist and this phase is explicitly activated.
objective: Make supported Python APIs deliberate at cohesive package and subpackage import surfaces without treating every defined implementation class as a supported export.
authorized_scope: After accepted prerequisite results and separate activation, inventory exact current supported imports and maintained deep-import consumers for each selected package surface.

Define explicit package and subpackage exports and `__all__` inventories that expose only supported contracts while allowing non-exported implementation classes to use descriptive non-private names under the accepted Phase 1 policy.
Preserve, stage, or retire existing supported imports only through the accepted compatibility decision, synchronized source, typing, tests, examples, API documentation, and migration records.
Create package-specific descendants later only where one cohesive export or compatibility boundary can be independently verified and closed.
completion_criteria: Every selected package and subpackage has one explicit supported import inventory with no accidental wildcard or root re-export leakage under the accepted contract.
Maintained consumers, tests, examples, and documentation use supported imports, and any retired path follows its explicitly accepted compatibility and migration disposition.

Public class, method, protocol, exception, enum, serializer, and result contracts remain synchronized with typing and documentation; unsupported deep accessibility is not misrepresented as a supported API.
Applicable conformance, import, wheel, typing, test, Sphinx, Harness, and projection checks pass with residual limitations reported and no automatic successor activation.
exclusions: Do not assume `__all__` prevents explicit deep imports or that package imports can control method visibility on an exported class.
Do not break an accepted public or serialized contract merely to reduce an export count, remove compatibility without authority, or introduce wildcard facade modules.
Do not move domain behavior, scientific policy, numerical policy, or persistence semantics while changing import ownership unless a separately authorized descendant includes that concern.
No protected execution, dependency change, release, staging, commit, push, or automatic activation is authorized by this inactive Task.
